newsitem.title: USA: Huge crowds pack San Francisco for gay parade.
newsitem.headline: Huge crowds pack San Francisco for gay parade.

text.p: Hundreds of thousands of people packed downtown San Francisco Sunday to watch the annual gay pride parade, a colourful and outrageous march featuring leather-clad bikers and cheerleaders in drag.
Up to 500,000 people were estimated at the event -- officially called the Lesbian Gay Bisexual Transgender Pride Parade and Celebration -- which is one of the biggest gay events in the world.
Thousands of people took part in the 27th annual parade, kicked off by leather-clad men and women riding motorcycles.
The parade included many scantily-clad men and women, others in outrageous costumes and a team of men dressed up as women cheerleaders with huge wigs.

Gymnasts, drum bands and theatre groups marched along Market Street between motorized cable cars, limousines and floats. The loud beat of disco music mingled with cheers, applause and the blaring of horns.
A number of AIDS support groups also marched in the parade. San Francisco's large gay community has been ravaged by AIDS (acquired immune deficiency syndrome).
Sightseers stood six deep on sidewalks decorated with balloons and rainbow-coloured gay freedom flags while others stood on fountains to get a better view.
San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown and several other local politicians rode in the parade.
"I have more fun in this parade than I do in any of the others," Brown told an interviewer on San Francisco's KOFY television, which broadcast the parade live.

Television announcers said the atmosphere at the event was more upbeat than it had been in recent years, attributing this partly to advances in drugs that are giving a new lease of life to people with AIDS.
